canonical_question: Does the 'correlation index above 0.99' for the fitting curves guarantee that the two-peak decomposition is physically unique, or could a three-peak model fit equally well?

question_variants.question: Does the 'correlation index above 0.99' for the fitting curves guarantee that the two-peak decomposition is physically unique, or could a three-peak model fit equally well?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The provided text states the fitting curves have a correlation index above 0.99 but does not contain evidence evaluating whether a three-peak model would fit equally well or if the two-peak decomposition is physically unique.

answers.answer: The text confirms the correlation index is above 0.99 but does not address the uniqueness of the two-peak model versus a three-peak model.
answers.boundary_limitation: No information on alternative models provided
evidence_spans: For the nitrogen-doped N-2 HEA, an additional low-temperature peak (blue curve) and two high-temperature peaks (green and magenta curves) were also observed (see Fig. 5C ).
The peak height of the additional low-temperature peak is 0.002, and that of the two high-temperature peaks is 0.027 and 0.009, respectively.
Hence, only ~5.3% of all the nitrogen atoms in the N-2 HEA contribute to the formation of ordered nitrogen complexes.
